summary: Describes role argument validation (since 2.11) via `meta/argument_specs.yml`, which inserts a validation task at the start of the role and fails it on invalid parameters. Specs in `meta/main.yml` also work but break below 2.11; dependencies are validated first; the inserted task is tagged `always`.
questions: How do I validate the variables passed to my role?
Where do I put a role's argument spec?
Can I put argument_specs in meta/main.yml?
Why does the argument validation task still run when I use --tags?
Do role dependencies get validated before my role?

answer_card.title: Role argument validation
answer_card.answer_md:
Since 2.11, define a spec in `meta/argument_specs.yml` (or `.yaml`). Ansible inserts a task at the start of the role that validates supplied parameters; if validation fails, the role fails.

Notes:
- Specs in `meta/main.yml` are supported but won't work below 2.11, so prefer `meta/argument_specs.yml`.
- If the role has dependencies, their validation runs first, even if the dependent role's validation then fails.
- The validation task is tagged `always`; for statically imported roles it runs unless you use `--skip-tags`.
